data.body:
# Phase 2 complete — fix landed through RED→GREEN with both mutations proven

Gerrit change **1981**. Commit `a102eeaf4d`.

## The fix, across the two files that had to move together

**`_commands/gates.py`** — `close_plan_review_gate_check` now binds the `gate_enabled`
result to `state` and, inside the unchanged `if not state:` skip branch, returns
`verdict="unreadable"` when `state is GateState.UNREADABLE` and `"disabled"` otherwise.
`ok` stays `True` for both: the fail-OPEN posture is untouched, only the reporting is
honest. Every payload the function returns — both skips plus `exempt`, `disposition`, the
validity result, and the `unavailable` exception path — now carries an explicit boolean
`gate_ran` stamp. A new public predicate `gates.gate_ran(check)` is its single reader.

**`_commands/transition_close.py`** — `if check.get("verdict") != "disabled":` became
`if gates.gate_ran(check):`. No verdict-string literal remains in that decision.

**Why a stamp rather than a wider comparison.** The ticket rejected
`not in ("disabled", "unreadable")` as "the same fragility with one more element", and it
is right: any list of skip strings has to be *remembered*. The producer instead records the
answer at the point where it is actually known, derived from `GateState`'s truthiness — so
the "did the gate run?" question is answered where `GateState` already lives, and a future
verdict is added at a return statement that must state its own `gate_ran`. An **unstamped**
payload answers `False`: fail-safe for the in-lock question, because absent evidence that
the gate ran must never authorise extra work inside the write lock.

## How the deferral test was re-anchored (not deleted)

`tests/unit/test_gate_state_tristate_f5c4.py` carried
`test_the_close_gate_caller_is_behaviourally_UNCHANGED_for_both_states`, which asserted
`off == unreadable` — i.e. it pinned the payload collapse **on purpose**, as f5c4's marker
that the split was deferred to this ticket.

Deleting it would have removed the guard written to catch exactly this transition. It is
instead **re-pointed at the behaviour it was guarding the way to**, as
`test_the_close_gate_reports_a_config_fault_distinctly_from_a_deliberate_disable`, with a
docstring recording that it previously pinned the opposite and why that is now discharged.
Its intent is unchanged — the close gate must not launder a FAULT into a POLICY CHOICE —
and it is strictly stronger than before: `off != unreadable` plus both exact verdicts, both
`ok is True`, both `gate_ran is False`, and the original source-level `is not` check kept.
The module went from 11 to 14 assertions; the other three tests in it are untouched.

## RED→GREEN

RED first, all three oracles, before any fix existed:

* `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_close_gate_unreadable_config_2091.py` — drives a **real
  close** under a malformed `rebar.toml`. RED on `verdict == "unreadable"` (got
  `"disabled"`). This is the coverage the Gerrit reviewer flagged as missing: the verdict
  was previously untested through the close path at all.
* `tests/unit/test_close_gate_ran_predicate_2091.py` — 5 RED (`AttributeError`/`KeyError`:
  the API did not exist).
* the re-anchored f5c4 guard — RED on the same collapse.

The fix was written by a subagent that **never saw any of them** — the files were moved out
of its tree, not merely omitted from its prompt, and it was handed only the contract. All
10 went GREEN against oracles it could not read.

## Mutation results — both hazards seeded, both caught

* **(a) verdict collapse** — restore `"verdict": "disabled"` for the unreadable case →
  **2 RED** (the close-path test and the re-anchored guard).
* **(b) the in-lock extra read** — restore `verdict != "disabled"` while KEEPING the split
  verdict, i.e. reconstruct the exact regression Gerrit LLM-Review caught on change 1975
  patchset 1 → **RED**: *"an unreadable config installed the in-lock recheck: the gate was
  consulted 2 times, so a config read happened INSIDE the write lock."*

Mutation (b) is the load-bearing one. The call-count assertion passes both before and after
the fix by design — it is a **regression pin**, and its teeth come from that mutation rather
than from a pre-fix RED.

## Proof that no previously-succeeding close now fails, and no extra in-lock read occurs

Observed at runtime, on a real store outside pytest, driving a real close with a malformed
config: status `closed`, gate consulted **exactly once**, payload
`{'ok': True, 'gate_ran': False, 'verdict': 'unreadable'}`. Identical call count to
`origin/main` (also 1). The `ok=True` fail-OPEN result is unchanged, so
`_raise_plan_review_close_gate_error` is still never reached on this path and no user-facing
message changed.

## Scope & safety

* **Caller sweep** — one production consumer of this verdict (`transition_close.py:492`).
  One *test* fake (`test_plan_review_close_gate_lifecycle.py`) had to start stamping
  `gate_ran: True`; its `checks == 2` assertion is untouched.
* **Restoration, not creation** — no new entry point, user-visible artifact, or mutating
  external call. `gates.gate_ran` is an internal predicate in a private module.
* **No new dependency** — the diff adds no import at all.
* **No test weakening** — the three other modified test files kept identical assertion
  counts (4/4, 10/10, 24/24); the exact-dict expectations gained the new key and remain
  exact-equality; no `skip`/`xfail` added anywhere.

## Siblings (Step 7) — swept both axes, none found

* **Construct axis.** Swept every `verdict` string comparison in `src/rebar` (14 sites) and
  confirmed each semantically. All the others ask about the verdict *itself*
  (`== "PASS"`, `== "certified"`, `!= "BLOCK"`), which is the string's actual job. Only the
  fixed site used a verdict string as a proxy for a **different** structural fact, and only
  it gated work inside a lock.
* **Parity axis.** Rule: *a gate that was skipped must neither claim a reason it does not
  have, nor install work under the write lock.* `gate_enabled` has three consumers. The two
  siblings — the plan-review START-WORK gate (`gates.py:270`, returns a bare `False`) and
  the completion-verification close gate (`close_precheck.py:563`, returns `None`) — are
  **N/A, not MISSING**: both return a sentinel that makes no claim about *why*, so there is
  no payload for a fault to be laundered into, and neither installs an in-lock closure. The
  close plan-review gate is the only one of the three that constructs a reason-bearing
  verdict payload.

## Residual risk

* **Accepted** — the completion-verification close gate cannot distinguish gate-off from
  config-unreadable either, but it returns `None` rather than a false claim, and
  `gate_enabled`'s stderr warning still makes the fault observable on all three paths. The
  fail-OPEN posture itself is a separate contested policy and explicitly out of scope here.
* **Accepted** — the new `unreadable` verdict is not added to `docs/plan-review-gate.md`.
  No enumerated verdict list exists there that goes stale, and the payload's `reason`
  string is self-describing.
* **None other observed.**
